digest.component_or_area: CI fetch and rebar store initialization
propositions: Full clone of tickets store costs 1.04 GiB / 59s wall; partial clone with blob:none filter reduces to 68.7 MiB / 14.3s (~15x reduction) while preserving complete commit ancestry needed for merge-base scoping
Rebar fetch occurs post-clone and cannot apply filters; the size lever is the actions/checkout step, not rebar-side flags
When tickets fetch times out via agent git proxy, rebar silently bootstraps a fresh orphan branch via worktree add --orphan, creating a diverged empty store that returns [] and diverges from origin
blob:none partial clone is safe for rebar access patterns (verify-identity, blame, authorship resolution) because they read event/keyring bodies from the working tree, not lazy blobs
Fail-open orphan-bootstrap (P1 bug 01e8-302b) requires fail-closed non-zero exit instead; faster fetch alone only lowers probability, does not fix the mechanism
gerrit-verify.yaml verify-identity job fetches full history (6.73m / 92% of job) despite complete commit graph being preserved under blob:none filter
